review_scope: All nine rows in contact-sheet.png and frame sequences; GIF files verified present. Animated temporal playback cannot be observed directly through static image tool, so cadence review uses displayed frame sequence.
identity: Gray fuzzy stitched plush baby elephant, peach inner ears, cream toes, short trunk, dark eyes preserved across states.
registration: Common foot ground across rows; intentional jumping displacement and failed slump preserved. No material scale-transition jump visible in standard contact sheet.

rows.evidence: Six frames keep grounded feet and face; eyes open, narrow, close and reopen. Calm blink is readable.
Eight right-facing frames alternate long extended limbs and passing poses; connected tail and trunk, stable ground.
Eight left-facing frames preserve rightward cadence temporal order through individual frame mirroring; no asymmetric prop.
Four poses progress from planted foreleg to raised greeting with visible toes, then lower again. Final foreleg remains slightly raised but forms a readable return toward first pose.
Five poses show anticipation, lift, highest airborne peak, descent, settle. Peak feet are visibly clear of ground; first/last ground registration agrees with idle.
Eight poses visibly slump by lowering head and ears, closing eyes in the middle and recovering; grounded feet and no detached tears/effects.
Six poses clasp forefeet expectantly and tilt head both ways, including blink. Upright stance is naturally taller; no limb disconnection.
Six grounded poses have focused head/trunk adjustments and alternating head tilt; reads as gentle processing rather than locomotion. Activity is deliberately subtle.
Six poses lower head and direct gaze downward, tilt to inspect and blink; grounded feet and consistent gray plush identity.

observations: No clipping, detached effects, stray props or guide marks visible.
Waving final pose is partway lowered; first-frame completion supplies return in loop.
Active-work motion is quiet head and trunk movement.
